001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jfr;
002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
005import java.net.URI;
006import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
007import java.nio.file.Path;
008
009import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
010
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.BufferHints;
015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter;
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.KeyValuesFormatterBuilder;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.WriteMethod;
020
021import jdk.jfr.Recording;
022
023/**
024 * A {@link LogOutput} that commits each log event as a JFR event (see
025 * {@link RainbowGumLogEvent}) instead of writing anywhere.
026 * <p>
027 * The output prefers {@link WriteMethod#STRING}, so formatter-backed encoders hand the
028 * formatted message directly to {@link #write(LogEvent, String)} without first turning it
029 * into bytes:
030 *
031 * <pre>{@code
032 * logging.appender.myappender.output.uri=jfr:///
033 * }</pre>
034 *
035 * Per-event-type enablement, thresholds, and stack trace capture are controlled the same
036 * way as any other JFR event, e.g. with {@code -XX:StartFlightRecording} or a
037 * {@code .jfc} settings file - not through Rainbow Gum properties. If a Flight Recorder
038 * session that enables the relevant event type is not running, {@link #write} does
039 * (cheaply) nothing.
040 * <p>
041 * If the configured URI has a real path (anything past the root {@code /}), this output
042 * instead starts and owns its own {@link Recording} writing directly to that file for as
043 * long as the output is open, with every event type unconditionally enabled:
044 *
045 * <pre>{@code
046 * logging.appender.myappender.output.uri=jfr:///var/log/myapp.jfr
047 * }</pre>
048 *
049 * In this mode JFR's own per-event enablement/threshold filtering is bypassed entirely -
050 * whether an event is captured is decided solely by Rainbow Gum's normal level resolver
051 * (the same one that already decides whether {@link #write} is called at all), not by JFR
052 * settings.
053 * <p>
054 * This output also implements {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder}, supplying (as an
055 * overridable default, see {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy#DEFAULT}) an encoder
056 * that renders the message followed by any key values, e.g. {@code some message -
057 * {key=value}} - no timestamp/level/logger prefix, since the JFR event already carries
058 * those as separate fields - so leaving {@code encoder} unset when {@code output=jfr:///}
059 * picks this up automatically instead of the default TTLL encoder formatting a whole line
060 * only to throw most of it away.
061 */
062public final class JfrLogOutput implements LogOutput, LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder {
063
064        /**
065         * JFR output URI scheme.
066         */
067        public static final String JFR_SCHEME = "jfr";
068
069        private static final URI JFR_URI = URI.create(JFR_SCHEME + ":///");
070
071        private static final LogFormatter KEY_VALUES_FORMATTER = new KeyValuesFormatterBuilder()
072                .format(KeyValuesFormatterBuilder.Format.LOGFMT)
073                .build();
074
075        /**
076         * Renders the message followed by any key values in logfmt, e.g. {@code some message
077         * - {key=value other="a b"}}, or just the message when there are none. Shared with
078         * {@link JfrAlertListener}, which renders alerts the same way.
079         */
080        static final LogFormatter MESSAGE_FORMATTER = LogFormatter.of((output, event) -> {
081                event.formattedMessage(output);
082                if (!event.keyValues().isEmpty()) {
083                        output.append(" - {");
084                        KEY_VALUES_FORMATTER.format(output, event);
085                        output.append('}');
086                }
087        });
088
089        private final URI uri;
090
091        private final @Nullable Path destination;
092
093        private volatile @Nullable Recording recording;
094
095        /**
096         * Creates a JFR output that emits events only for whatever externally started Flight
097         * Recorder session (if any) is currently running, without managing a recording of its
098         * own.
099         */
100        public JfrLogOutput() {
101                this(JFR_URI, null);
102        }
103
104        /**
105         * Creates a JFR output.
106         * @param uri the output's own configured URI, returned as-is by {@link #uri()}.
107         * @param destination if not null, a file this output starts and owns its own
108         * {@link Recording} against for as long as the output is open (see {@link #start},
109         * {@link #close}); if null, events are only captured by whatever externally started
110         * recording (if any) is already running.
111         */
112        public JfrLogOutput(URI uri, @Nullable Path destination) {
113                this.uri = uri;
114                this.destination = destination;
115        }
116
117        /**
118         * Extracts a recording destination file from a configured output URI, if any. The
119         * default {@code jfr:///} URI has path {@code "/"} (root, no real path segment),
120         * which must not be mistaken for a configured destination file.
121         * @param uri configured output URI.
122         * @return destination file, or null if {@code uri} has no real path.
123         */
124        static @Nullable Path destinationOrNull(URI uri) {
125                String path = uri.getPath();
126                if (path == null || path.length() <= 1) {
127                        return null;
128                }
129                return Path.of(path);
130        }
131
132        @Override
133        public URI uri() {
134                return uri;
135        }
136
137        @Override
138        public void start(LogConfig config) {
139                var path = destination;
140                if (path == null) {
141                        return;
142                }
143                var r = new Recording();
144                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.TraceEvent.class);
145                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.DebugEvent.class);
146                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.InfoEvent.class);
147                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.WarnEvent.class);
148                r.enable(RainbowGumLogEvent.ErrorEvent.class);
149                try {
150                        r.setDestination(path);
151                }
152                catch (IOException e) {
153                        r.close();
154                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
155                }
156                r.start();
157                this.recording = r;
158        }
159
160        @Override
161        public OutputType type() {
162                return OutputType.MEMORY;
163        }
164
165        @Override
166        public BufferHints bufferHints() {
167                return WriteMethod.STRING;
168        }
169
170        @Override
171        public LogEncoder encoder(String name, LogConfig config) {
172                return LogEncoder.of(MESSAGE_FORMATTER).provide(name, config);
173        }
174
175        @Override
176        public void write(LogEvent event, String s) {
177                switch (event.level()) {
178                        case TRACE -> emitTrace(event, s);
179                        case DEBUG -> emitDebug(event, s);
180                        case INFO -> emitInfo(event, s);
181                        case WARNING -> emitWarn(event, s);
182                        case ERROR -> emitError(event, s);
183                        case ALL, OFF -> {
184                        }
185                }
186        }
187
188        /*
189         * One method per event type, each allocating its event and never returning it, so the
190         * JIT can eliminate the allocation when the event is disabled. A factory returning
191         * the event merges the five allocations into one value, which defeats escape
192         * analysis: measured 40 bytes and about 14 ns per call with no recording, against
193         * none and about 1.5 ns this way. The methods are here, not on RainbowGumLogEvent:
194         * verifying a method of the event base class that refers to its subclasses loads them
195         * while the base class is still being linked, and JFR fails to instrument an event
196         * class loaded then when a recording is already running (-XX:StartFlightRecording).
197         */
198        private static void emitTrace(LogEvent event, String s) {
199                var e = new RainbowGumLogEvent.TraceEvent();
200                if (e.isEnabled()) {
201                        fill(e, event, s);
202                        e.commit();
203                }
204        }
205
206        private static void emitDebug(LogEvent event, String s) {
207                var e = new RainbowGumLogEvent.DebugEvent();
208                if (e.isEnabled()) {
209                        fill(e, event, s);
210                        e.commit();
211                }
212        }
213
214        private static void emitInfo(LogEvent event, String s) {
215                var e = new RainbowGumLogEvent.InfoEvent();
216                if (e.isEnabled()) {
217                        fill(e, event, s);
218                        e.commit();
219                }
220        }
221
222        private static void emitWarn(LogEvent event, String s) {
223                var e = new RainbowGumLogEvent.WarnEvent();
224                if (e.isEnabled()) {
225                        fill(e, event, s);
226                        e.commit();
227                }
228        }
229
230        private static void emitError(LogEvent event, String s) {
231                var e = new RainbowGumLogEvent.ErrorEvent();
232                if (e.isEnabled()) {
233                        fill(e, event, s);
234                        e.commit();
235                }
236        }
237
238        private static void fill(RainbowGumLogEvent e, LogEvent event, String s) {
239                e.message = s;
240                e.logger = event.loggerName();
241                e.throwable = stackTraceOrNull(event);
242        }
243
244        static @Nullable String stackTraceOrNull(LogEvent event) {
245                var t = event.throwableOrNull();
246                if (t == null) {
247                        return null;
248                }
249                var stackTrace = new StringBuilder();
250                ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(stackTrace, t);
251                return stackTrace.toString();
252        }
253
254        @Override
255        public void write(LogEvent event, byte[] bytes, int off, int len, ContentType contentType) {
256                var charset = contentType.charsetOrNull();
257                if (charset == null) {
258                        charset = StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
259                }
260                write(event, new String(bytes, off, len, charset));
261        }
262
263        @Override
264        public void flush() {
265        }
266
267        @Override
268        public void close() {
269                var r = recording;
270                if (r != null) {
271                        r.close();
272                }
273        }
274
275}
